neighbours.label: The second word of a fixed social-science or ecology term or journal title headed by 'population' or 'family' (population viability, Population Bulletin, Family Relations), vs the head noun used freely
fire: A population viability model predicted the frogs could vanish within fifty years.
The paper estimated the population attributable fraction of deaths from air pollution.
Her article on aging was published in Population Bulletin.
The survey appeared in the journal Family Relations in 2003.
Managers used population viability analysis to set a hunting quota for the deer.
That report in Population Bulletin tracked migration to the cities.
Smoking had the largest population attributable risk for lung disease.
A study in Family Relations looked at how siblings share chores.
quiet: A habitat suitability model predicted the frogs could vanish within fifty years.
The paper estimated the share of deaths from air pollution in each city.
Her article on aging was published in a local newspaper.
The survey asked each family about their relations with neighbors.
Managers counted the population of deer before setting a hunting quota.
That report on the viability of the new railway was shelved.
Smoking had the largest effect on the risk of lung disease.
A study of family meals looked at how siblings share chores.
